CanonicalMolecularIdentity.name: CanonicalMolecularIdentity
CanonicalMolecularIdentity.description: Normalize a molecular record under explicit, auditable identity policies. Args: smiles (str): RDKit-readable SMILES; disconnected components are retained. fragment_policy (str): ``keep_all`` preserves every component; ``largest_organic`` picks the carbon-containing fragment with most heavy atoms (canonical-SMILES lexical tie break), falling back to the largest fragment among all components if none contains carbon. This is NOT charge neutralization. tautomer_policy (str): ``preserve`` or RDKit ``canonical`` tautomer; canonical tautomer does not mean the dominant solution species. keep_stereo (bool): Keep assigned stereochemical labels by default. Returns: dict: Canonical selected SMILES, original component SMILES, selected and original formula/charge, chiral center labels, policy and RDKit version. Atom indexes refer to the normalized selected molecule.

ElementwiseNumericOperations.output_description:
Apply one declared arithmetic operation to a numeric vector or matrix.

Args:
    operation: add/subtract/multiply/divide use values as the left operand.
        sqrt/log/exp/reciprocal/abs are unary. log is the natural logarithm.
    values: A nonempty 1D vector or nonempty rectangular 2D matrix, with at
        most 10000 total finite real entries in scientific row/column order.
        Ragged, mixed vector/matrix, empty rows and deeper nesting fail.
        Booleans/null/strings are rejected. Arithmetic is ordinary float64,
        not arbitrary-precision integer or symbolic arithmetic.
    other: For binary operations, either one finite numeric scalar broadcast
        to every row, or a finite vector of EXACTLY the same length. A
        one-element list is not broadcast. For a 2D matrix, other may be
        a scalar or an exactly matching rectangular 2D matrix; 1D vectors,
        single-row/column broadcasting and all implicit axis expansion fail. Unary operations require null.

Returns:
    dict with operation, values (same ordered shape, all finite floats),
    length (outer length), shape, element_count, operand_mode
    (unary/scalar_broadcast/aligned_vector/aligned_matrix), and scope.
    No file, network, code generation, expression evaluation, model fitting
    or unit inference occurs. Callers must establish compatible quantities,
    record alignment and meaningful transformations from scientific context.

Raises:
    ValueError: Invalid length/type/operation, zero division, negative square
        root, nonpositive logarithm, overflow/nonfinite result, or a nonzero
        multiply/divide/exp result that underflows to zero. Failing element
        indices are zero-based row-major indices.
        Entire calls fail; invalid rows are not dropped, clipped or imputed.

        Ragged, mixed vector/matrix, empty rows and deeper nesting fail.
        Booleans/null/strings are rejected. Arithmetic is ordinary float64,
        not arbitrary-precision integer or symbolic arithmetic.
    other: For binary operations, either one finite numeric scalar broadcast
        to every row, or a finite vector of EXACTLY the same length. A
        one-element list is not broadcast. For a 2D matrix, other may be
        a scalar or an exactly matching rectangular 2D matrix; 1D vectors,
        single-row/column broadcasting and all implicit axis expansion fail. Unary operations require null.

        Entire calls fail; invalid rows are not dropped, clipped or imputed.

Returns: dict: Canonical selected SMILES, original component SMILES, selected and original formula/charge, chiral center labels, policy and RDKit version. Atom indexes refer to the normalized selected molecule.

CanonicalMolecularIdentity.name: CanonicalMolecularIdentity
CanonicalMolecularIdentity.description: Normalize a molecular record under explicit, auditable identity policies. Args: smiles (str): RDKit-readable SMILES; disconnected components are retained. fragment_policy (str): ``keep_all`` preserves every component; ``largest_organic`` picks the carbon-containing fragment with most heavy atoms (canonical-SMILES lexical tie break), falling back to the largest fragment among all components if none contains carbon. This is NOT charge neutralization. tautomer_policy (str): ``preserve`` or RDKit ``canonical`` tautomer; canonical tautomer does not mean the dominant solution species. keep_stereo (bool): Keep assigned stereochemical labels by default. Returns: dict: Canonical selected SMILES, original component SMILES, selected and original formula/charge, chiral center labels, policy and RDKit version. Atom indexes refer to the normalized selected molecule.

CompareMolecularFingerprints.name: CompareMolecularFingerprints
CompareMolecularFingerprints.description: Return an explicit symmetric pairwise fingerprint similarity/distance matrix. Input is 2-100 SMILES records, kept separately so disconnected molecules are never split on dots. Supported bit/count algorithms: morgan, rdkit, atom_pair, torsion, maccs, avalon, pharm2d, secfp, tautomer_target; minhash MHFP is excluded. metric is tanimoto or dice; count vectors use RDKit's count-vector definition. distance=true returns 1-score. Score1 is reported normally and does not prove structural identity. Index labels preserve every supplied record.

MatchedPeriodicDisplacements.name: MatchedPeriodicDisplacements
MatchedPeriodicDisplacements.description:
Return minimum-image displacements for fixed same-index crystal sites.

CIF fractional positions are preserved without rational-coordinate snapping.

Both explicitly uploaded ordered structures must contain the same species
sequence, 1..256 sites and a common cell (absolute entry tolerance 1e-8 A).
No atom permutation, rigid alignment, strain removal or trajectory unwrapping
is performed. Cell rows are lattice vectors. For atom i displacement is
mobile_cart[i] + image_shift[i] @ reference_cell - reference_cart[i].
Fractional source coordinates must be finite with abs<=1e6. Volume>=1e-8 A^3
and perpendicular cell heights>=1e-5 A are required. Exact reciprocal-height
bounds enumerate at most 1e6 total image candidates; exceeding this rejects
the entire call before enumeration. No [-1,1] assumption is made for skew
cells. Images within 1e-8 A of the minimum are treated as tied: the
lexicographically smallest image is returned, with tie_count and unique flag.
A half-cell displacement therefore need not have a unique direction.
Source SHA256 identifies actual input bytes. This geometric primitive does
not infer diffusion, atomic identity correspondence, or a physical pathway.

PeriodicNeighborList.name: PeriodicNeighborList
PeriodicNeighborList.description:
Return all directed periodic geometric neighbors in a finite radius.

CIF fractional positions are preserved without rational-coordinate snapping.

Args:
    structure_file: Explicitly uploaded ordered crystal file, same public
        allowlist and10MiB source limit as the other crystal primitives.
    cutoff_angstrom: Finite positive Cartesian radius<=10angstrom. Search
        uses pymatgen's periodic neighbor algorithm, including image shifts
        beyond[-1,1] when required by an oblique cell. At most256 source
        sites and10000 returned directed edges; estimated candidate work
        N²*product(2*ceil((cutoff+1e-8)/h_i)+3) must be<=1000000,where h_i
        are perpendicular cell heights. Excess work/edges reject the whole
        call before return; results are never truncated to the edge limit.

Returns:
    dict with neighbors(list of unique edge_id,center_index,neighbor_index,image_shift,
    distance_angstrom,displacement_angstrom),edge_count,source SHA/formula,
    species,cell_angstrom,cutoff_angstrom,boundary_tolerance_angstrom,
    candidate_pair_bound andscope. Cell vectors are rows. Displacement is
    r_neighbor+image_shift@cell-r_center (center to neighbor-image).
    The list is directed: reverse edges are retained,and same-atom nonzero
    images are valid neighbors. Only the exact self pair with zero image
    is removed; coincident distinct sites are not silently discarded.
    Distances<=cutoff+1e-8angstrom are included. No chemical bonding,
    coordination-shell,oxidation-state or nearest-neighbor interpretation.

Raises:
    ValueError: Unsupported type/radius,disorder,too many sites or images,
        near-singular/nonfinite cell,nonfinite or abs>1e6 fractional
        coordinates,numerical failure or>10000 edges.

Apply one declared arithmetic operation to a numeric vector or matrix.

Args:
    operation: add/subtract/multiply/divide use values as the left operand.
        sqrt/log/exp/reciprocal/abs are unary. log is the natural logarithm.
    values: A nonempty 1D vector or nonempty rectangular 2D matrix, with at
        most 10000 total finite real entries in scientific row/column order.
        Ragged, mixed vector/matrix, empty rows and deeper nesting fail.
        Booleans/null/strings are rejected. Arithmetic is ordinary float64,
        not arbitrary-precision integer or symbolic arithmetic.
    other: For binary operations, either one finite numeric scalar broadcast
        to every row, or a finite vector of EXACTLY the same length. A
        one-element list is not broadcast. For a 2D matrix, other may be
        a scalar or an exactly matching rectangular 2D matrix; 1D vectors,
        single-row/column broadcasting and all implicit axis expansion fail. Unary operations require null.

Returns:
    dict with operation, values (same ordered shape, all finite floats),
    length (outer length), shape, element_count, operand_mode

    record alignment and meaningful transformations from scientific context.

        indices are zero-based row-major indices.
        Entire calls fail; invalid rows are not dropped, clipped or imputed.

SolveLinearProgram.name: SolveLinearProgram
SolveLinearProgram.description: Optimize an explicit continuous linear objective subject to supplied equalities, inequalities and bounds. Return verified primal/dual witnesses in original units or an explicit infeasible/unbounded/numerical failure.
SolveLinearProgram.call_signature: SolveLinearProgram(objective: list, bounds: list, inequality_matrix: list | None=None, inequality_rhs: list | None=None, equality_matrix: list | None=None, equality_rhs: list | None=None, direction: str='min') -> dict

parameters.name: objective
parameters.description: Ordered1..500 finite real coefficients c of the REQUESTED objective c dot x. Internally divide by max(abs(c)) or1 for an all-zero objective. Nonzero normalized coefficients require abs>=1e-8; unsupported dynamic ranges fail with a rescaling hint. Boolean/string/null/nonfinite cells fail. Caller owns scientific variable definitions, units and order.

parameters.name: bounds
parameters.description: Exactly one explicit[lower,upper]pair per variable; finite endpoints have abs<=1e12. null means an unbounded endpoint, never zero. No implicit nonnegativity or broadcasting; fixed variables are allowed but lower cannot exceed upper.

parameters.name: inequality_matrix
parameters.description: Rows of A_ub in A_ub*x<=b_ub, width exactly objective length. Jointly null with RHS or aligned lists;[],[]means no rows. Each row and RHS is internally divided by max(abs(row)),or abs(RHS),or1 for a zero row. Nonzero normalized coefficients require abs>=1e-8. Combined equality/inequality limits:2000rows and100000coefficients.

parameters.name: inequality_rhs
parameters.description: Finite inequality RHS values aligned to source rows. After positive row scaling, nonzero RHS magnitude must be in1e-8..1e12; unsupported ranges fail explicitly. Transform BOTH sides to represent greater-than constraints. Marginals are reversed to original RHS units.

parameters.name: equality_matrix
parameters.description: Rows of A_eq in A_eq*x=b_eq, width exactly objective length; jointly null with RHS or aligned lists. Positive numerical row scaling and normalized coefficient guards are the same as for inequalities. No scientific normalization constraint, conservation law or intercept is inserted.

parameters.name: equality_rhs
parameters.description: Finite equality RHS values in the same row order. After positive row scaling, nonzero RHS magnitude must be in1e-8..1e12. Caller establishes the continuous model; returned marginals use original RHS units.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: min minimizes the requested objective, max maximizes it. Objective value and all returned marginals use this requested direction, including sign reversal from the internal minimization for max.

lower_bound_marginals.description: Derivative of REQUESTED optimum with respect to lower endpoints; nonnegative for min and nonpositive for max. Unbounded endpoints have numerically zero marginal.

upper_bound_marginals.description: Derivative of REQUESTED optimum with respect to upper endpoints; nonpositive for min and nonnegative for max.

dual_objective.description: RHS dot marginals plus finite-bound endpoints dot their marginals, in requested-objective units. Null endpoints contribute no term.

scaled_primal_violation.description: Maximum scaled inequality/equality/bound feasibility violation, also checking zero marginals for nonexistent endpoints.

dual_sign_violation.description: Maximum sign violation for inequality and finite-bound marginals after accounting for min/max direction.

scaled_complementarity_violation.description: Maximum absolute slack-times-marginal, scaled by1+absolute requested objective.

scaled_duality_gap.description: Absolute requested primal-minus-dual objective divided by1+absolute primal+absolute dual.

ElementwiseNumericOperations.name: ElementwiseNumericOperations
ElementwiseNumericOperations.description: Apply one explicitly selected arithmetic transformation to a finite vector or matrix, preserving shape and order. Validate operand shape, mathematical domain and finite representability; do not generate code.

parameters.name: operation
parameters.description: One exact operation: add/subtract/multiply/divide are binary with values on the left; sqrt/log(natural)/exp/reciprocal/abs are unary. No formulas,code or eval.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: Ordered1D vector or nonempty rectangular2D matrix with at most10000total finite entries. No ragged/mixed/deeper shapes. Arithmetic uses float64,not arbitrary precision; bool/null/string/nested arrays rejected. Row IDs/order and scientifically compatible units must be established by caller.

PeriodicNeighborList.name: PeriodicNeighborList
PeriodicNeighborList.description:
Return all directed periodic geometric neighbors in a finite radius.

CIF fractional positions are preserved without rational-coordinate snapping.

Args:
    structure_file: Explicitly uploaded ordered crystal file, same public
        allowlist and10MiB source limit as the other crystal primitives.
    cutoff_angstrom: Finite positive Cartesian radius<=10angstrom. Search
        uses pymatgen's periodic neighbor algorithm, including image shifts
        beyond[-1,1] when required by an oblique cell. At most256 source
        sites and10000 returned directed edges; estimated candidate work
        N²*product(2*ceil((cutoff+1e-8)/h_i)+3) must be<=1000000,where h_i
        are perpendicular cell heights. Excess work/edges reject the whole
        call before return; results are never truncated to the edge limit.

Returns:
    dict with neighbors(list of unique edge_id,center_index,neighbor_index,image_shift,
    distance_angstrom,displacement_angstrom),edge_count,source SHA/formula,
    species,cell_angstrom,cutoff_angstrom,boundary_tolerance_angstrom,
    candidate_pair_bound andscope. Cell vectors are rows. Displacement is
    r_neighbor+image_shift@cell-r_center (center to neighbor-image).
    The list is directed: reverse edges are retained,and same-atom nonzero
    images are valid neighbors. Only the exact self pair with zero image
    is removed; coincident distinct sites are not silently discarded.
    Distances<=cutoff+1e-8angstrom are included. No chemical bonding,
    coordination-shell,oxidation-state or nearest-neighbor interpretation.

Raises:
    ValueError: Unsupported type/radius,disorder,too many sites or images,
        near-singular/nonfinite cell,nonfinite or abs>1e6 fractional
        coordinates,numerical failure or>10000 edges.

ElementwiseNumericOperations.output_description:
Apply one declared arithmetic operation to a numeric vector or matrix.

Args:
    operation: add/subtract/multiply/divide use values as the left operand.
        sqrt/log/exp/reciprocal/abs are unary. log is the natural logarithm.
    values: A nonempty 1D vector or nonempty rectangular 2D matrix, with at
        most 10000 total finite real entries in scientific row/column order.
        Ragged, mixed vector/matrix, empty rows and deeper nesting fail.
        Booleans/null/strings are rejected. Arithmetic is ordinary float64,
        not arbitrary-precision integer or symbolic arithmetic.
    other: For binary operations, either one finite numeric scalar broadcast
        to every row, or a finite vector of EXACTLY the same length. A
        one-element list is not broadcast. For a 2D matrix, other may be
        a scalar or an exactly matching rectangular 2D matrix; 1D vectors,
        single-row/column broadcasting and all implicit axis expansion fail. Unary operations require null.

Returns:
    dict with operation, values (same ordered shape, all finite floats),
    length (outer length), shape, element_count, operand_mode

    record alignment and meaningful transformations from scientific context.

        multiply/divide/exp result that underflows to zero. Failing element
        indices are zero-based row-major indices.
        Entire calls fail; invalid rows are not dropped, clipped or imputed.

FitParametricCurve.output_description:
Fit one declared fixed curve family using bounded local least squares.

Families/formula/parameter order are public REGISTRY. There are2 or3 fitted
parameters, at most1000 observations, and observations must exceed parameter
count. Duplicate x observations are allowed; at least2 distinct x are needed.
Optional sigma are positive observation standard deviations, not weights;
residuals are divided by sigma. No weights are estimated. Absolute_sigma
affects approximate covariance scaling only. Bounds may narrow but never
widen family domains; per-entry null means the family's default bound.
Linear, soft_l1 or huber loss uses fixed f_scale1 in sigma-scaled units.
Return local optimizer diagnostics even when not converged; success only
means numeric termination, never global optimum or scientific applicability.
Approximate local covariance is supplied only for converged, full-column-rank,
interior linear-loss fits with residual df>0. It assumes independent errors,
a locally adequate model and supplied sigma conventions. Active bounds,
robust losses, nonconvergence or deficient rank return null covariance/SE.
No confidence interval, extrapolation validity or model-selection claim.

model.description: Selected family,exact formula,ordered fitted parameter names/values and observed x range; no task acceptance decision.

sample_count.description: Number of observed x/y pairs,duplicates retained.

residual_degrees_of_freedom.description: n minus parameter count,strictly positive; nuisance fitting is not ignored.

predictions.description: Model response values aligned with input x,original response units.

residuals.description: Prediction minus observed y in original input row order,response units.

residual_convention.description: Exact residual sign and unit convention.

residual_sum_squares.description: Sum of squared unweighted response residuals,response units squared.

scaled_residual_sum_squares.description: Sum of squared residual/sigma; unit relative sigma if omitted. Robust losses still report this ordinary squared diagnostic separately from objective.

rmse.description: sqrt(unweighted RSS/n),original response units; not residual standard error sqrt(RSS/df).

optimizer.description: SciPy local termination code/message,convergence flag,evaluation count,optimality,active-bound signs and loss; numeric convergence does not prove global optimum or scientific adequacy.

jacobian_rank.description: Numerical column rank of optimizer residual Jacobian,using machine-epsilon*max(shape)*largest singular-value cutoff. For robustloss Jacobian is the SciPy loss-modified approximation.

jacobian_singular_values.description: Descending singular values of local residual Jacobian; scale/unit dependent.

jacobian_condition_number.description: Largest/smallest singular-value ratio for full-column-rank Jacobian; null if deficient. Numeric conditioning is distinct from scientific identifiability.

parameter_covariance.description: Approximate k×k local covariance under explicit independent-error/linear-loss/interior/rank conditions; otherwise null. Units follow parameter products.

parameter_standard_errors.description: Square roots of local covariance diagonal,ordered parameter units; null when covariance unavailable. No confidence interval coverage claim.

covariance_status.description: Explicit reason local covariance is available or omitted; robustloss/bounds/nonconvergence/rankdeficiency are not silently treated as valid Wald inference.

sigma_mode.description: unit_relative when omitted,relative when supplied with residual-variance scaling,absolute when explicitly true.

scope.description: Scientific limits of local curve fitting/evaluation.

upper_bound_marginals.description: Derivative of REQUESTED optimum with respect to upper endpoints; nonpositive for min and nonnegative for max.

dual_objective.description: RHS dot marginals plus finite-bound endpoints dot their marginals, in requested-objective units. Null endpoints contribute no term.

scaled_primal_violation.description: Maximum scaled inequality/equality/bound feasibility violation, also checking zero marginals for nonexistent endpoints.

dual_sign_violation.description: Maximum sign violation for inequality and finite-bound marginals after accounting for min/max direction.

scaled_complementarity_violation.description: Maximum absolute slack-times-marginal, scaled by1+absolute requested objective.

scaled_duality_gap.description: Absolute requested primal-minus-dual objective divided by1+absolute primal+absolute dual.

arguments.code:
truth = [[0,1,2,3],[1,2,3,4],[-1,0,1,2]]
pred = [[[0.1,1.1,2.1,3.1],[1.2,2.2,3.2,4.2],[1.0,2.0,3.0,4.0]],[[0.5,1.5,2.5,3.5],[1.5,2.5,3.5,4.5],[-0.5,0.5,1.5,2.5]],[[1.0,2.0,3.0,4.0],[1.0,2.0,3.0,4.0],[-0.6,0.4,1.4,2.4]]]
nominal = [0.9,0.05,0.05]
bounds = [[0.2,0.9],[0.05,0.7],[0.05,0.6]]
cohort_mse = [[sum((pred[m][c][s]-truth[c][s])**2 for s in range(4))/4.0 for c in range(3)] for m in range(3)]
vertices = [[bounds[i][bi] if t==i else bounds[j][bj] if t==j else 1.0 - bounds[i][bi] - bounds[j][bj] for t in range(3)] for i in range(3) for j in range(i+1,3) for bi in range(2) for bj in range(2)]
vertices = [w for w in vertices if all(w[t] >= bounds[t][0]-1e-12 and w[t] <= bounds[t][1]+1e-12 for t in range(3))]
risk_matrix = [[sum(cohort_mse[m][t]*w[t] for t in range(3)) for w in vertices] for m in range(3)]
worst_risks = [max(risk_matrix[m]) for m in range(3)]
worst_weights = [[w for z,w in zip(risk_matrix[m], vertices) if abs(z - worst_risks[m]) < 1e-12][0] for m in range(3)]
nominal_risks = [sum(cohort_mse[m][t]*nominal[t] for t in range(3)) for m in range(3)]
witness_risks = [sum(cohort_mse[m][t]*worst_weights[m][t] for t in range(3)) for m in range(3)]
robust_selected = [['a','b','c'][m] for m in range(3) if abs(worst_risks[m] - min(worst_risks)) <= 1e-9]
nominal_selected = [['a','b','c'][m] for m in range(3) if abs(nominal_risks[m] - min(nominal_risks)) <= 1e-9]
print('cohort_mse', cohort_mse)
print('worst_risks', worst_risks)
print('nominal_risks', nominal_risks)
print('witness_risks', witness_risks)
print('robust_selected', robust_selected)
print('nominal_selected', nominal_selected)

NumericRangeMask.output_description:
Return an ordered 0/1 indicator for a declared finite numeric range.

Accept a nonempty finite 1D vector or rectangular 2D matrix, with at most
10000 total cells. Boolean/null cells, ragged or higher-dimensional input
are rejected. Bounds are finite numbers or null; null is unbounded, never
a missing-cell replacement. Inclusive flags must be actual booleans.
A reversed range is an error. Equal endpoints with either endpoint open
produce a valid all-zero mask. Two null bounds produce an all-one mask.
Output numeric 0/1 preserves every input position and shape. No rows are
deleted and no values are imputed. It does not infer a scientific cutoff,
establish statistical significance, or correct sampling/measurement bias.

QueryScientificRecordsFile.name: QueryScientificRecordsFile
QueryScientificRecordsFile.description: Filter, project and stably order a public JSON record file with explicit predicates and a typed string/integer identity field. Preserve source provenance and write complete output plus a bounded preview.
QueryScientificRecordsFile.call_signature: QueryScientificRecordsFile(records_file: str, id_field: str, predicates: list | None=None, fields: list | None=None, order_by: list | None=None, limit: int | None=None, preview_limit: int=20) -> dict

parameters.name: records_file
parameters.description: Uploaded or current-task artifact JSON file. Accepts a record list, or an object with a data list, containing 0–60,000 rows and at most 25 MiB. Private files and shared artifact directories are not readable.

parameters.name: id_field
parameters.description: Literal source identity key; every source ID must be a unique nonempty string or integer, with no implicit type conversion.

parameters.name: predicates
parameters.description: Null or up to 32 AND conditions. Each has field and op; binary operators require value and unary operators omit it. Missing predicate fields raise except for exists/missing. Null numeric comparisons return false. Validation precedes filtering, so condition order cannot hide malformed data.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Null keeps all fields. Otherwise provide up to 256 distinct top-level field names. The identity field is always retained. Missing requested fields in selected rows raise; explicit null values remain null.

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description: Null or up to 8 distinct sort keys. Each key has field, optional direction (ascending/descending), and optional nulls (first/last). Missing fields or mixed non-null scalar families raise. Equal keys retain source order.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Null retains all matches. An integer from 0 to 60,000 limits rows after filtering and sorting. Full matching count and artifact output count are reported separately.

parameters.name: preview_limit
parameters.description: Return 0–100 complete preview rows within a 20,000-character budget. This does not change the full artifact. If a row exceeds the preview budget, omit it and report truncation; never return malformed partial JSON.

predictions.failure_reason: PlanningFailure: ValueError: PlannerStopped: Cannot form a scientifically valid scaffold-overlap graph with the registered capabilities. Available: MurckoDecompose(smiles) is a per-SMILES primitive that returns only the scaffold string (canonical_smiles/kekule/mol_block) with NO carrying of record_id or split, so per-record for_each/collect yields only an ordered list of scaffold strings; QueryScientificRecordsFile/FilterRecords produce or filter record-object tables (record_id, smiles, split) but cannot attach a computed scaffold field; AggregateRecordGroups can group records by a key column (and its group_count would give distinct nonempty scaffold count) but only if a 'scaffold' field already exists on the records; FilterRecords 'in' would need such a column too; no zip/join/positional-array-alignment, set-intersection, or labeled group-by primitive is registered (SetOverlap reported unknown, and prior searches for a join/zip or scaffold-group tool returned nothing). Thus validation_ids_sharing_training_scaffold (validation record_ids whose NONEMPTY Bemis–Murcko scaffold occurs among NONEMPTY training scaffolds) and distinct_nonempty_scaffold_count (distinct nonempty scaffolds over all records) cannot both be derived from actual node outputs without copying file/preview values into literals or substituting an invalid method (e.g., molecular fingerprints, substructure containment, or hypergeometric enrichment). Needed capability: either (a) a record-level scaffold annotation tool that maps a record table (record_id, smiles, split) to record objects augmented with the ring-and-linker Bemis–Murcko canonical scaffold string (empty scaffolds preserved as empty), or (b) a labeled group-by/set-overlap primitive taking record_id/split/scaffold arrays that ignores empty values and returns validation IDs whose nonempty scaffold is present in the nonempty training scaffold set plus the distinct nonempty scaffold count.

QueryScientificRecordsFile.name: QueryScientificRecordsFile
QueryScientificRecordsFile.description: Filter, project and stably order a public JSON record file with explicit predicates and a typed string/integer identity field. Preserve source provenance and write complete output plus a bounded preview.
QueryScientificRecordsFile.call_signature: QueryScientificRecordsFile(records_file: str, id_field: str, predicates: list | None=None, fields: list | None=None, order_by: list | None=None, limit: int | None=None, preview_limit: int=20) -> dict

parameters.name: records_file
parameters.description: Uploaded or current-task artifact JSON file. Accepts a record list, or an object with a data list, containing 0–60,000 rows and at most 25 MiB. Private files and shared artifact directories are not readable.

parameters.name: id_field
parameters.description: Literal source identity key; every source ID must be a unique nonempty string or integer, with no implicit type conversion.

parameters.name: predicates
parameters.description: Null or up to 32 AND conditions. Each has field and op; binary operators require value and unary operators omit it. Missing predicate fields raise except for exists/missing. Null numeric comparisons return false. Validation precedes filtering, so condition order cannot hide malformed data.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Null keeps all fields. Otherwise provide up to 256 distinct top-level field names. The identity field is always retained. Missing requested fields in selected rows raise; explicit null values remain null.

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description: Null or up to 8 distinct sort keys. Each key has field, optional direction (ascending/descending), and optional nulls (first/last). Missing fields or mixed non-null scalar families raise. Equal keys retain source order.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Null retains all matches. An integer from 0 to 60,000 limits rows after filtering and sorting. Full matching count and artifact output count are reported separately.

parameters.name: preview_limit

        most 10000 total finite real entries in scientific row/column order.
        Ragged, mixed vector/matrix, empty rows and deeper nesting fail.
        Booleans/null/strings are rejected. Arithmetic is ordinary float64,
        not arbitrary-precision integer or symbolic arithmetic.
    other: For binary operations, either one finite numeric scalar broadcast
        to every row, or a finite vector of EXACTLY the same length. A
        one-element list is not broadcast. For a 2D matrix, other may be
        a scalar or an exactly matching rectangular 2D matrix; 1D vectors,
        single-row/column broadcasting and all implicit axis expansion fail. Unary operations require null.

Returns:
    dict with operation, values (same ordered shape, all finite floats),
    length (outer length), shape, element_count, operand_mode
    (unary/scalar_broadcast/aligned_vector/aligned_matrix), and scope.

    or unit inference occurs. Callers must establish compatible quantities,
    record alignment and meaningful transformations from scientific context.

        root, nonpositive logarithm, overflow/nonfinite result, or a nonzero
        multiply/divide/exp result that underflows to zero. Failing element
        indices are zero-based row-major indices.
        Entire calls fail; invalid rows are not dropped, clipped or imputed.

document.observation_model: Controlled exact label-count probabilities for the two carbon positions of neutral ethanol. Listed13C substitutions are exact isotope labels in the molecular graphs. No other isotope or natural-abundance convolution contributes. The mass instrument resolves the number of13C atoms but cannot distinguish positional isomers with the same exact mass; compare the exact molecular masses of all listed graphs to verify the observation groups.
document.analysis_policy: First remove the NMR datum and derive the sharp possible site1 enrichment interval from only the complete mass-count histogram and nonnegative joint fractions. Then restore the independent site1 enrichment and reconstruct all four joint state fractions. Covariance of site indicators is P(both)-P(site1)*P(site2).
document.scope: Analytical isotope-position identifiability, not an isotope-production procedure, metabolic pathway flux claim or instruction to create labeled biological material.

FitParametricCurve.output_description:
Fit one declared fixed curve family using bounded local least squares.

Families/formula/parameter order are public REGISTRY. There are2 or3 fitted
parameters, at most1000 observations, and observations must exceed parameter
count. Duplicate x observations are allowed; at least2 distinct x are needed.
Optional sigma are positive observation standard deviations, not weights;
residuals are divided by sigma. No weights are estimated. Absolute_sigma
affects approximate covariance scaling only. Bounds may narrow but never
widen family domains; per-entry null means the family's default bound.
Linear, soft_l1 or huber loss uses fixed f_scale1 in sigma-scaled units.
Return local optimizer diagnostics even when not converged; success only
means numeric termination, never global optimum or scientific applicability.
Approximate local covariance is supplied only for converged, full-column-rank,
interior linear-loss fits with residual df>0. It assumes independent errors,
a locally adequate model and supplied sigma conventions. Active bounds,
robust losses, nonconvergence or deficient rank return null covariance/SE.
No confidence interval, extrapolation validity or model-selection claim.

initial_parameters.description: Exact finite ordered parameters for selected public family. Must satisfy bounds; scientific initial choice belongs to caller. No task-specific initial values hidden in tool.

lower_bounds.description: Null for public family defaults, or exact ordered entries; null entry retains family lower bound. Finite entries may narrow but cannot widen family domain.

upper_bounds.description: Null for public family defaults, or exact ordered entries; null entry retains family upper bound. Finite entries may narrow but cannot widen family domain.

sigma.description: Null for unit relative residual scale, or aligned strictly positive finite observation standard deviations; residuals divided by sigma,not multiplied. No weights inferred.

absolute_sigma.description: Boolean covariance convention: true requires explicit sigma treated absolute; false scales approximate covariance by scaled RSS/residual df. Does not change optimizer objective.

loss.description: linear squared residual,soft_l1 orhuber on sigma-scaled residuals,fixed f_scale=1. Robust-loss covariance is explicitly unavailable.

FitParametricCurve.output_description:
Fit one declared fixed curve family using bounded local least squares.

Families/formula/parameter order are public REGISTRY. There are2 or3 fitted
parameters, at most1000 observations, and observations must exceed parameter
count. Duplicate x observations are allowed; at least2 distinct x are needed.
Optional sigma are positive observation standard deviations, not weights;
residuals are divided by sigma. No weights are estimated. Absolute_sigma
affects approximate covariance scaling only. Bounds may narrow but never
widen family domains; per-entry null means the family's default bound.
Linear, soft_l1 or huber loss uses fixed f_scale1 in sigma-scaled units.
Return local optimizer diagnostics even when not converged; success only
means numeric termination, never global optimum or scientific applicability.
Approximate local covariance is supplied only for converged, full-column-rank,
interior linear-loss fits with residual df>0. It assumes independent errors,
a locally adequate model and supplied sigma conventions. Active bounds,
robust losses, nonconvergence or deficient rank return null covariance/SE.
No confidence interval, extrapolation validity or model-selection claim.

rmse.description: sqrt(unweighted RSS/n),original response units; not residual standard error sqrt(RSS/df).

optimizer.description: SciPy local termination code/message,convergence flag,evaluation count,optimality,active-bound signs and loss; numeric convergence does not prove global optimum or scientific adequacy.

jacobian_rank.description: Numerical column rank of optimizer residual Jacobian,using machine-epsilon*max(shape)*largest singular-value cutoff. For robustloss Jacobian is the SciPy loss-modified approximation.

jacobian_singular_values.description: Descending singular values of local residual Jacobian; scale/unit dependent.

parameter_covariance.description: Approximate k×k local covariance under explicit independent-error/linear-loss/interior/rank conditions; otherwise null. Units follow parameter products.

parameter_standard_errors.description: Square roots of local covariance diagonal,ordered parameter units; null when covariance unavailable. No confidence interval coverage claim.

covariance_status.description: Explicit reason local covariance is available or omitted; robustloss/bounds/nonconvergence/rankdeficiency are not silently treated as valid Wald inference.

sigma_mode.description: unit_relative when omitted,relative when supplied with residual-variance scaling,absolute when explicitly true.

scope.description: Scientific limits of local curve fitting/evaluation.

arguments.code:
obs=[[100.0,19.384615384615383,3.2769230769230773,'train'],[200.0,17.79310344827586,5.617241379310344,'train'],[500.0,12.0,8.04,'train'],[1000.0,7.2,6.42,'train'],[1500.0,5.6,4.8133333333333335,'validation'],[2500.0,4.615384615384615,3.084923076923077,'validation']]
cands=[['tau_1000us_nodc',0.001,False],['tau_1000us_dc',0.001,True],['tau_2000us_nodc',0.002,False],['tau_2000us_dc',0.002,True],['tau_4000us_nodc',0.004,False],['tau_4000us_dc',0.004,True]]
eps0=8.8541878128e-12
thr=1e-06
train=[o for o in obs if o[3]=='train']
val=[o for o in obs if o[3]=='validation']
print('n_train='+str(len(train)))
print('train_omegas='+str([o[0] for o in train]))
print('train_roles='+str([o[3] for o in train]))
print('n_val='+str(len(val)))
print('val_omegas='+str([o[0] for o in val]))
print('val_roles='+str([o[3] for o in val]))
wmin=min(o[0] for o in obs)
print('smallest_omega_rad_s='+str(wmin))
results=[]
for c in cands:
    tau=c[1]
    nc=3 if c[2] else 2
    rows=[]
    rhs=[]
    for o in train:
        x=o[0]*tau
        a=1.0/(1.0+x*x)
        if nc==3:
            rows=rows+[[1.0,a,0.0]]
        else:
            rows=rows+[[1.0,a]]
        rhs=rhs+[o[1]]
    for o in train:
        x=o[0]*tau
        a=1.0/(1.0+x*x)
        if nc==3:
            rows=rows+[[0.0,a*x,1.0/o[0]]]
        else:
            rows=rows+[[0.0,a*x]]
        rhs=rhs+[o[2]]
    M=[]
    for i in range(nc):
        row=[sum(rows[k][i]*rows[k][j] for k in range(len(rows))) for j in range(nc)]
        M=M+[row+[sum(rows[k][i]*rhs[k] for k in range(len(rows)))]]
    ok=True
    for col in range(nc):
        piv=col
        best=abs(M[col][col])
        for r in range(col+1,nc):
            if abs(M[r][col])>best:
                best=abs(M[r][col])
                piv=r
        if best<=0.0:
            ok=False
        tmp=M[col]
        M[col]=M[piv]
        M[piv]=tmp
    coef=[0.0]*nc
    if ok:
        for col in range(nc):
            for r in range(col+1,nc):
                f=M[r][col]/M[col][col]
                for j in range(col,nc+1):
                    M[r][j]=M[r][j]-f*M[col][j]
        for i in range(nc-1,-1,-1):
            s=M[i][nc]
            for j in range(i+1,nc):
                s=s-M[i][j]*coef[j]
            coef[i]=s/M[i][i]
    nonneg=ok and all(v>=0.0 for v in coef)
    maxerr=0.0
    for o in val:
        x=o[0]*tau
        a=1.0/(1.0+x*x)
        pr=coef[0]+coef[1]*a
        if nc==3:
            pl=coef[1]*a*x+coef[2]/o[0]
        else:
            pl=coef[1]*a*x
        maxerr=max(maxerr,abs(pr-o[1]),abs(pl-o[2]))
    keep=nonneg and maxerr<=thr
    if keep:
        why='retained'
    elif not ok:
        why='singular_fit_rejected'
    elif not nonneg:
        why='negative_parameter_rejected'
    else:
        why='validation_threshold_exceeded'
    results=results+[[c[0],tau,nc,coef[0],coef[1],(coef[2] if nc==3 else 0.0),maxerr,keep,why]]
sup=[r[0] for r in results if r[7]]
print('candidate_screen='+str(results))
print('supported_model_ids='+str(sup))
print('n_supported='+str(len(sup)))
surv=[r for r in results if r[7]]
if len(surv)==1:
    tau_s=surv[0][1]
    eps_i=surv[0][3]
    delta=surv[0][4]
    kap=surv[0][5]
    eps_st=eps_i+delta
    dc_c=eps0*kap
    xm=wmin*tau_s
    rl=delta*xm/(1.0+xm*xm)
    dl=kap/wmin
    frac=dl/(rl+dl) if (rl+dl)!=0.0 else 0.0
    dc_req=not any((r[2]==2) and r[7] for r in results)
    print('relaxation_time_s='+str(tau_s))

FitBulkRNASeqCounts.name: FitBulkRNASeqCounts
FitBulkRNASeqCounts.description: Fit a PyDESeq2 negative-binomial bulk RNA-seq count model with explicit design factors/contrast and sample-ID mapping. Uses nonnegative integer gene-by-sample counts, matched metadata, declared Cook filtering and model-resource versions. This is a fitted count-model analysis, distinct from generic p-value adjustment or enrichment; cache identity includes data/model settings.

inputs.notes: Explicit nonnegative integer gene-by-sample count source.
Explicit sample-ID metadata matched to counts.

1..6 unique categorical metadata columns for additive intercept-plus-factor effects. Each factor must vary, categorical coding must be full rank with >=2 residual degrees of freedom. No continuous covariates/interactions/random effects. Additive factor order has no scientific meaning and is lexically canonicalized before coding/fitting/cache identity.
Exactly [factor,tested_level,reference_level]; the signed log2 fold change is tested/reference. Factor must be in design and each contrasted level must have >=2 fitted samples.
Metadata column containing exact sample identities, default sample_id. Cannot be a design factor.
Count TSV column containing unique nonempty gene identities, default gene_id; all other columns are sample counts.
Explicit suffix required on every metadata sample ID, then removed exactly once for matching count sample IDs. Empty preserves exact IDs. No implicit name cleanup.
Null fits all count samples. Otherwise >=4 unique exact count sample IDs, canonicalized to original column order; all input genes remain in the fitting universe.
Requested PyDESeq2 dispersion trend parametric(default) or mean. Actual fallback and warnings are returned, never hidden.
Apply library Cook distance p-value filtering, default true. Count replacement remains false and independent filtering remains false regardless.
Default true. Reuse numerical model results keyed by input bytes, parameters, package versions and implementation SHA; still write a fresh task-local result artifact. No gold-answer cache.

outputs.notes: Full all-gene result artifact;model metadata and source identity retained.
Preview rows only;full hypothesis family remains in results_file.

data.unknown_truth_model: Each row is a fixed joint population stratum defined by the two predictions and one weak label. An unknown binary true label can be distributed arbitrarily inside every stratum, with no homogeneity or deterministic label assumption. The unknown amount of mass in a row whose truth differs from its weak label lies between0 and that row mass. Error budgets are absolute probability mass over the entire population, not error fractions conditional on the agreement group. Sum weak-label error mass across all agreement rows at most the agreement bound, and separately across all disagreement rows at most the disagreement bound. The SAME unknown truth allocation must underlie both predictors and every paired risk contrast.
data.research_scope: Project-authored exact population probability law and sensitivity assumptions, not finite observation counts, annotation measurements or error rates certified by data. Risk is expected binary disagreement with the unknown truth. No sampling uncertainty, integer latent counts, independence of label errors or causal interpretation is stipulated.
data.question_policy: Find sharp attainable intervals for both predictor risks and for risk_A minus risk_B under the shared ambiguity set. Decide whether either predictor has strictly smaller risk for EVERY admissible common truth allocation. Report overlapping marginal intervals separately from uniform relative ordering; overlap of individually optimized intervals does not answer the paired ordering question. A label budget is an assumption for sensitivity analysis, not a conclusion about the weak annotator.
data.units: Probability fractions. Numeric answers within1e-8 absolute plus1e-7 relative. Interval entries are [minimum,maximum]. The strict uniform-order decision is exact.

provenance.kind: Project-authored controlled probability sensitivity panel, not measured labels or a real annotation audit.
provenance.method_context: Sharp bounded linear functionals over a shared latent-truth polytope. Common latent variables retain coupling; separate marginal risk bounds are not difference bounds.

        not arbitrary-precision integer or symbolic arithmetic.
    other: For binary operations, either one finite numeric scalar broadcast
        to every row, or a finite vector of EXACTLY the same length. A

        single-row/column broadcasting and all implicit axis expansion fail. Unary operations require null.

        Entire calls fail; invalid rows are not dropped, clipped or imputed.

document.policy: Unweighted polynomial least squares includes every power0throughdegree. For candidates whose every leave-one-out training design has full column rank, compute predictions by refitting after leaving out each whole row and average squared errors. PRESS residual/(1-h_ii) is an equivalent computation when its denominator is nonzero. A candidate that loses full column rank on any leave-one-out split has no unique ordinary least-squares leave-one-out prediction and is ineligible; report null, not zero or an arbitrary minimum-norm extrapolation. Ties within1e-10 use smaller degree.
document.scope: Four fixed controlled readings. The score concerns this leave-one-out protocol only; endpoint omissions can test extrapolation relative to a fold. It is not independent deployment validation.
document.answer_contract_note: The nullable MSE fields are required because full-rank eligibility must be checked.

records_file.description: Uploaded or current-task artifact JSON file. Accepts a record list, or an object with a data list, containing 0–60,000 rows and at most 25 MiB. Private files and shared artifact directories are not readable.

id_field.description: Literal source identity key; every source ID must be a unique nonempty string or integer, with no implicit type conversion.

predicates.description: Null or up to 32 AND conditions. Each has field and op; binary operators require value and unary operators omit it. Missing predicate fields raise except for exists/missing. fields.description: Null keeps all fields. Otherwise provide up to 256 distinct top-level field names. The identity field is always retained. Missing requested fields in selected rows raise; explicit null values remain null.

order_by.description: Null or up to 8 distinct sort keys. Each key has field, optional direction (ascending/descending), and optional nulls (first/last). Missing fields or mixed non-null scalar families raise. Equal keys retain source order.

limit.description: Null retains all matches. An integer from 0 to 60,000 limits rows after filtering and sorting. Full matching count and artifact output count are reported separately.

failure_feedback.invalid_input: status=error, error_type=InvalidInput; inspect the argument error and query DescribeTools for the contract.
failure_feedback.invalid_output: status=error, error_type=InvalidOutput; no contract-invalid or nonfinite result is accepted as scientific evidence.
failure_feedback.missing_resource: status=blocked, error_type=MissingResource or MissingEnvironment; configure the declared dependency.
failure_feedback.external_source: Remote failures, missing scientific data and pending jobs are reported explicitly; no fallback value is invented.
failure_feedback.retired_name: status=error, error_type=RetiredTool with active replacement names and explicit migration guidance; incompatible signatures are never silently aliased.

document.model: Each report estimates the SAME unknown fixed voltage theta: y_i=theta+loading_i*z+epsilon_i. z and all epsilon_i have zero mean, are mutually independent, and have the stated known variances. Report values are one realized panel. There are no unknown variance components to estimate.
document.pooling_policy: Among ALL linear unbiased estimates sum_i w_i*y_i with sum_i w_i=1, minimize the true variance. Signed weights are allowed: they are coefficients of estimators, not physical mixture fractions. Preserve source report order for the returned weights.
document.comparison_policy: The proposed independence report uses inverse-MARGINAL-variance weights (including each shared-offset contribution on its diagonal) but ignores every off-diagonal covariance. Its reported variance is the reciprocal of the sum of these marginal precisions. Separately compute the ACTUAL variance of that SAME naive-weight estimator under the true joint model. Do not compare the naive reported variance with the optimal estimator variance as if they described one estimator.

provenance.data_origin: Explicitly constructed numerical instrument/reporting studies for this benchmark; not measurements from a named laboratory or archive.
provenance.method_scope: Conditional finite-dimensional linear measurement models. Scientific conclusions follow from the stated covariance/distance definitions; no distributional or causal interpretation beyond those assumptions.
